events.title: One union across industries
events.body: Delegates meet at Brand’s Hall to found an organization that seeks worker power across trades, industries and national backgrounds. Bill Haywood calls the convention to order.

events.title: An organizing foothold in the mining West
events.body: The IWW and Western Federation of Miners organize miners alongside service and construction workers. Economic crisis, employer resistance and federal troops help unravel their gains.

events.title: Immigrant workers challenge the steel-car industry
events.body: The Pressed Steel Car Company dispute becomes a major test of organizing across languages. IWW involvement helps bring national attention to workers’ demands and violent repression.

events.title: The street corner becomes a battleground
events.body: IWW speakers challenge restrictions on public organizing. Arrests turn the right to speak into a collective campaign, with Elizabeth Gurley Flynn among its prominent organizers.

events.title: Organizers fill Spokane’s jails
events.body: Wobblies defy restrictions on street speaking in a campaign tied to their fight against exploitative employment agencies. Imprisonment and conditions inside the jails become organizing issues.

events.title: A free-speech fight in farm country
events.body: Organizers travel to Fresno to challenge restrictions on public meetings. The campaign confronts imprisonment and attacks on the union’s ability to organize agricultural workers.

events.title: The Lawrence textile strike
events.body: A pay cut brings immigrant textile workers into a mass walkout. Organizing across languages, strike relief and public pressure help win wage gains in the struggle remembered as Bread and Roses.

events.title: Speech meets police and vigilante violence
events.body: A downtown speaking ban leads to a prolonged confrontation. IWW members and allies face arrests and violence while defending their ability to meet and organize in public.

events.title: The strike also becomes a prisoner-defense campaign
events.body: Joseph Ettor, Arturo Giovannitti and striker Joseph Caruso are imprisoned on murder charges during the Lawrence conflict. Their case makes legal defense part of the wider labor struggle.

events.title: Silk workers sustain a long strike
events.body: Workers across Paterson’s silk industry pursue shorter hours and better conditions. The strike loses, but its mass meetings and public campaign leave an enduring record of worker organization.

events.title: Local 8 builds interracial power on the waterfront
events.body: Black and white longshore workers organize together in Local 8. Ben Fletcher helps lead a union that challenges employers’ use of racial and ethnic division.

events.title: A deadly confrontation in the hop fields
events.body: A clash at the Durst Ranch leaves four people dead and exposes harsh agricultural labor conditions. The aftermath brings imprisonment and a wider debate over labor camps.

events.title: Utah executes Joe Hill
events.body: The IWW songwriter is executed after a disputed murder conviction. His case becomes a lasting focus of labor memory, protest and prisoner solidarity.

events.title: Gunfire at the Everett waterfront
events.body: At least five Wobblies and two deputies die when boats carrying IWW supporters reach Everett. Seventy-four Wobblies face murder-conspiracy charges; Thomas Tracy’s acquittal is followed by the release of the other defendants.

events.title: Timber workers demand a different working day
events.body: A regional strike pushes for shorter hours and better camp conditions across the Pacific Northwest. Spokane is shown as a regional organizing reference, not the site of every strike.

events.title: Workers are forcibly removed from Bisbee
events.body: An armed roundup seizes striking miners and others. More than a thousand people are transported out of Arizona and left in New Mexico, without normal legal proceedings.

events.title: Frank Little is lynched
events.body: Masked attackers seize the IWW organizer in Butte and hang him from a railroad trestle. Little had been supporting striking miners and opposing the war.

events.title: Federal agents raid the IWW nationwide
events.body: Federal raids seize union records and publications across the country. Chicago’s national headquarters becomes a focal point of the campaign that leads to mass prosecution.

events.title: A mass trial sends organizers to prison
events.body: The Chicago prosecution ends in convictions and long sentences for IWW organizers. Government surveillance, seized correspondence and union publications feature in the campaign against the defendants.

events.title: Centralia: violence, lynching and a contested trial
events.body: An Armistice Day confrontation at the IWW hall leaves four Legionnaires dead. Wesley Everest is later taken from jail and lynched; surviving Wobblies face murder prosecutions.

events.title: Internal conflict compounds repression
events.body: Disputes over leadership and organization culminate in a split at the Chicago convention. The IWW survives, but the rupture weakens a movement already battered by prosecution and employer opposition.
